summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to ₹269 crore, but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹45 crore (16.8% margin) and PAT dropped to ₹0.7 crore after one-offs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 6% YoY to ₹269 crore on higher volumes and tariff escalation. EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% a year ago, driven by higher transport/hiring costs at the CIDCO site, employee costs rising to 34% of revenue, and about ₹10 crore of deferred Q4 FY26 disposal work. The PCMC WtE plant was shut after a July 8 landslide of legacy waste that killed nine people, and management flagged a ₹22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) as an exceptional item. The company also refinanced ₹140 crore of Antony Lara's term loan from 10.25% to 8.25%, with a ₹7 crore prepayment charge.

segments.name: Collection & Transportation (C&T)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹156 crore, up 10% YoY; share of revenue 62% vs 60% a year ago. Management said margins are under pressure from repairs and maintenance and ageing contracts.

segments.name: MSW Processing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹75 crore, up 3% YoY; share 28%, flat. Growth slowed because the CIDCO bio-mining contract ended, and processing volumes rose 5% to about 0.85 million tons.

segments.name: Waste-to-Energy (PCMC)
segments.commentary: Plant suspended after the July 8 incident. Over 20 million green units generated in the quarter before the shutdown; restart expected by first/second week of October. Fixed costs of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (about ₹7 crore total) will run through the quarter.

segments.name: Construction & Demolition recycling
segments.commentary: Running at 600-650 tons per day against 600 tons per day capacity (±10%), with a 96% recycling rate, after BMC policy required large builders to send waste to the plant.

guidance_outlook: Management calls the Q1 margin compression transitional. It expects margins to recover toward the historical trend, with C&T margins improving after transport renegotiation and the labour-cost escalation pass-through.
Employee costs were 34% of revenue vs a historical 30-31%; management expects normalisation within about three quarters, so FY28 margins should be back at historical levels.
New volumes: the BMC contract adds about 1,500 tons per day from Q3 (only one ward live so far); the Atkoli project adds 600-800 tons per day from Q3/Q4. Q4 is the test of the full run-rate.
Growth from the existing portfolio is estimated at 6-9%, with new contracts adding 10-15%. Revenue from new contracts typically takes 2-3 quarters after LOA to reach the P&L.
Greater Noida EMS road sweeping contract: ₹243 crore over 5 years plus a 2-year extension option; starts Q3 FY27 with about ₹46 crore revenue in year one.
Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa and Kurnool) projects: land possession obtained, civil work under way, financial closure near final; the company says it is on schedule.
Impairment of ₹22-24 crore on the WtE assets is expected, before any insurance recovery; more detail is due with Q2 results. Auditors have flagged the plant-damage cost as an open item.
capex_capacity: PCMC WtE plant: suspended after the July 8 event; restart pending structural/safety assessment and OEM/Hitachi certification, expected by early October. The MRF and composting operation restarted on July 28 at about 400 tons per day.
Andhra Pradesh WtE projects (Kadapa and Kurnool): land possessed, civil contractor mobilised at Kadapa, Kurnool expected to start in about two weeks; the company said the project is on schedule.
Atkoli processing project in Thane: operational by Q4 FY27, adding 600-800 tons per day in processing.
Borrowings rose about ₹22 crore QoQ at gross level, for the AP WtE project and the new BMC C&T contract.
RDF sales of about 40,000 tons fell 28% YoY, partly because the CIDCO bio-mining project has been completed. Compost sales were stable at about 6,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Processing tonnage was 0.85 million tons (+5% YoY); C&T tonnage 0.55 million tons (+6% YoY); total about 1.4 million tons (+5%).
RDF net realisation is above ₹300 per ton, up from about ₹250 a year earlier.
Tipping fees range from ₹1,800 to ₹4,200 per ton, depending on scope, vehicle count and contract duration. Some C&T contracts (Thane, Jhansi, Varanasi) are billed per household or trip, not per ton.
Management says about 80% of operating costs are covered by escalation clauses, but the escalation lags cost increases by about six months.
Cost headwinds cited: fuel volatility, repairs and maintenance, additives and gases (linked to the Gulf/Hormuz conflict), plus a new Maharashtra DA revision and a Labour Code restatement.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the PCMC WtE operations and near-term revenue impact, given it is a high-margin business?
qa_highlights.answer: MRF and composting restarted July 28 at about 400 tons/day. WtE plant expected back by first/second week of October; fixed cost of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (about ₹7 crore) sits on the books meanwhile. Tipping fees continue, but power generation and sale revenue is hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did processing revenue growth moderate, and what is the margin trajectory from Q2/Q3 given cost inflation and wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Slowdown is due to the CIDCO bio-mining contract ending (a two-year project). Atkoli going live by Q4 restores growth. Transport and hiring costs pressured C&T margins; renegotiation with transport vendors should give some respite. Labour DA pressure is timing-related, with relief expected in H2 FY27 via escalations. Management says FY27 margins should move back toward historical trend, plus or minus a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Size of the Lara refinancing, the ₹15 crore court-linked receivable, and the Andhra project status?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹140 crore was refinanced at a lower rate. The ₹15 crore receivable is still pending with the Corporation after a favourable court judgement. Andhra: land possessed at Kadapa and Kurnool, JFE India has completed civil designs, civil contractor mobilised at Kadapa, Kurnool to start in about two weeks, financial closure nearly final.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹10 crore CIDCO cost recurring, and what is the payback on the refinancing (prepayment charge was ₹7 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹10 crore was closure-related disposal cost of inert material for the completed CIDCO bio-mining contract, and is not expected to recur. On refinancing, management cited a 15-year tenor and net benefit of about ₹14 crore after a ₹6 crore prepayment charge; the ₹7 crore figure in the PAT disclosure differs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is RDF sales volume down 28%, and what is realisation per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a timing issue, with new customers being added and sales from PCMC as well as CIDCO and Kanjurmarg. Net realisation is above ₹300 per ton versus about ₹250 a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What are the C&T revenue per ton and the segment margin, and is the business mix shifting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give per-ton or segment EBITDA for C&T. Some contracts (Thane, Jhansi, Varanasi) are billed per household or trip, and tipping fees range ₹1,800-4,200 per ton. Mix target is moving from about 70:30 C&T to processing toward 50:50, with processing/WtE the margin-accretive focus.

qa_highlights.question: What volumes do the new contracts add, and what is the test quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: BMC adds about 1,500 tons/day (only one ward live, 7 days of operation so far). Atkoli adds 600-800 tons/day from Q3 or Q4. Q4 is the test of full run-rate volumes. Management also confirmed no further one-offs expected beyond the WtE event.

risks_watch: PCMC WtE restart timing (first/second week of October) and the ₹7 crore fixed cost drag through Q2, plus the ₹22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) with details deferred to Q2 results; auditors have flagged the plant-damage cost as open.
Employee costs at 34% of revenue vs 30-31% historically; management expects normalisation in about three quarters, with escalations lagging costs by about six months.
C&T margin pressure from R&M, ageing contracts and transport/hiring costs; transport renegotiation outcome is unconfirmed.
Input-cost volatility (fuel, additives, gases linked to the Gulf conflict) against escalation coverage of about 80% of operating costs.
Execution on new volumes: BMC ramp-up (only one of seven wards live), Atkoli operational by Q4 FY27, and Andhra WtE projects (Kurnool start pending).
Borrowings up about ₹22 crore QoQ; weighted cost of debt ~10.1% expected to fall post refinancing. Pending ₹15 crore court-linked receivable from the Corporation.
Kanjurmarg legal matter (Supreme Court/High Court proceedings) raised by an investor; management said it sees no change in project location.
key_quotes: We view this quarter's profitability as transitional rather than the structural thing given the one-off nature of both the transportation cost deferral and the refinancing charge.
So the internal threshold should be to go back to our historical margin trend, but yes, it can be a plus or minus a quarter here and there.
So, in Q4 would be your test of the total volumes that we handle.
It was not completely anticipated. There were 2 factors that led to it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and firm that Q1 margin compression is transitional and largely one-off, but cautious and at times evasive on specifics: it declined to give C&T per-ton revenue or segment margin, and gave only a range on the WtE impairment and restart. Management said the escalation timing and the WtE shutdown will weigh on Q2.
